candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate response to medications, monitor adverse effects, and implement medication-specific precautions during recovery.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — sugammadex reversal and post-blockade respiratory/hemodynamic monitoring
candidate.educational_objective: After sugammadex reversal, continue respiratory and hemodynamic surveillance and maintain ventilatory support until adequate spontaneous respiration and airway patency are confirmed.

options.A: Discontinue ventilatory support immediately because sugammadex guarantees complete reversal with the injection.
options.B: Continue respiratory and hemodynamic monitoring and maintain ventilatory support until adequate spontaneous breathing and a patent airway are assured.
options.C: Avoid monitoring heart rate because sugammadex does not cause clinically important bradycardia.
options.D: Expect sugammadex to provide postoperative analgesia while neuromuscular function returns.

candidate.rationale: The current sugammadex label states that ventilatory support is mandatory until adequate spontaneous respiration is restored and the ability to maintain a patent airway is assured. It also warns of marked bradycardia, including rare cardiac arrest, within minutes after administration and of hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis. Therefore B is correct. A assumes immediate guaranteed recovery and removes support too early. C contradicts the hemodynamic-monitoring warning. D assigns an analgesic effect that is not the indication of sugammadex.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sugammadex reverses rocuronium/vecuronium blockade, but respiratory support and monitoring must continue until adequate spontaneous ventilation and airway patency are established; hemodynamic monitoring remains important because marked bradycardia can occur.
candidate.source_document_title: Sugammadex Injection / BRIDION (sugammadex) Injection — Full Prescribing Information
candidate.source_locator: Indications: reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium or vecuronium. Warnings 5.2 Marked Bradycardia: monitor hemodynamic changes; marked bradycardia/cardiac arrest reported within minutes. Sections 5.3–5.4 Respiratory Function Monitoring/Risk of Prolonged Blockade: ventilatory support is mandatory until adequate spontaneous respiration is restored and patent airway is assured; provide ventilation if blockade persists or recurs.

candidate.stem: A client receives sugammadex to reverse rocuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade after surgery. Which nursing action remains essential during recovery?
